boundaries: Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.
completion_conditions: The quarry has been killed, moved or contained away from the traveller route and Oren has checked whether passage is safe. Alternatively, the hunt has ended with the party back out of danger and Oren records the route as still unsafe or only temporarily deterred; merely admitting it is unfinished during an ongoing hunt does not close it.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.
gm_guidance.railroading: Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

facts.fact: The party stands above a shallow forest hollow. Below, a Rift-touched boar digs at a mineral seep beside the blocked trail.
Guild observer Oren Pike waits nearby with a rolled canvas and a sack of bitter feed. The boar has not noticed the party.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: One deliberate monster confrontation where preparation changes the danger.

objectives.description: Make the trail safe by killing, diverting or containing the quarry.
objectives.title: Choose the ground

opening_direction: Begin at the overlook with the quarry visible. Describe the trough, side path and fresh gouges; offer time for a plan before any charge.
premise: A Rift-touched boar has made a supply trail impassable. Choose your ground before the hunt becomes a charge.

branches: Ambush from cover rewards preparation but leaves the animal an escape route.
Relocation using feed and a clear exit can resolve the whole contract without combat.
A direct challenge gives the player control of position but exposes them to the initial rush.
consequences: An accurate route notice improves Guild trust. Exaggerating a temporary deterrent as a permanent cure risks later complaints, described in the closing scene rather than a compulsory sequel.
Oren pays for the achieved outcome. Keep any harvested trophy mundane unless the selected Ruleset supports a declared item.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.
dynamic_encounter_guidance: Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.
planned_encounters: One quarry. Solo level-one baseline: young Rift-touched boar, AC 11, HP 13, speed 30 ft, initiative +0; tusk +3 to hit, 1d6+1 piercing, one attack. If it traverses at least twenty clear feet toward its target before hitting, use a declared situational damage adjustment only if supported; otherwise present the charge as movement plus its ordinary tusk attack. No automatic stun, regeneration or hidden second phase. It withdraws at 4 HP if an exit exists. Add toughness or use the full referenced creature only for a stronger party after inspecting their actual state. Resolve attacks and any save using the admitted tools.
situations: Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Oren Pike, route observer: speaks in distances and wind direction. He wants the trail usable and offers 15 gp for a verified safe reopening, whether or not the animal dies. He refuses to serve as bait. His equipment can be lent without bargaining.
The quarry is an injured animal guarding a reliable feeding place. Its aggression is territorial, not a secret curse to be solved after combat.

Read the ground. The seep lies in a muddy bowl twenty feet across. A fallen trunk offers a waist-high barrier at one end; a narrow side path reaches an empty depression downwind. Gouges on the trunk show that the animal charges in a straight line and struggles to turn in mud. Show these signs plainly.

Preparation. A robust rope across the narrow approach, a barricade of fallen limbs or feed placed away from the trail can change where the first contact happens. Ask for a consequential check only when the setup is risky or hurried. Establish the actual benefit before the animal reaches it: lost movement, a blocked route or a diverted approach, according to admitted rules. It is not free damage.

The choice. Oren accepts a nonlethal outcome if the party can explain how travellers will pass safely. Simply frightening the boar back into cover is temporary success worth half the payment and an honest warning. Diverting it toward another occupied camp moves the harm and fails the contract once discovered.

After the charge. The animal tries to regain the seep or escape through the side path. If wounded and offered room, it leaves. Oren checks the route afterward, thanks the hunter and posts an accurate notice. The encounter ends without a hidden handler, second monster or mandatory tracking expedition.
